complete_package_official.package: v231 Linear (L-EM3 K=2) complete root + A-GR1 Attention, v195 Attention body unchanged
complete_package_official.note: Exact seconds and score unknown; no prediction is written. Parent v231 official reading was 291s against the 300s limit (9s of headroom).

what_this_timeout_settles: The v234 log left exactly one unknown: how far v234 overshot. v234's parent had 8s of headroom and this candidate's parent has 9s, so a 1s improvement was the entire available room, and the promotion rule recorded here before submission was conditional on v234's overshoot being at most 1s. This reading closes that question in the negative: the overshoot exceeds 1s. The two timeouts together now bracket the mechanism from both sides, and no near-neighbour Linear parent can rescue it. This is consistent with the property asserted at archiving time -- A-GR1's extra cost is calibration-side (6 layers x 32 steps of Adam) and carries no new operator on the deployed dynamic path, so it does not track the Linear parent.
decision: REJECTED. The preregistered promotion rule is settled on its timeout branch: an official score above the current root's 18518 inside 300s would promote; a timeout or a lower score does not, and this is the timeout. The root is unchanged at v231 (18518/291s) and the fallback root is unchanged at v233 (18428/288s). The implementation is closed: no step/window/candidate-count retry, and it is not transplanted into any other candidate. The A-GR1 mechanism itself is not closed -- only this way of landing it.

sibling_evidence_recorded_after_archivin.event: the v234 complete package (v230 root + the same A-GR1 block) was reported by the user as an official TIMEOUT (>300s) on 2026-09-10, after this card was built and archived
sibling_evidence_recorded_after_archivin.impact_on_this_candidate: A-GR1's extra cost is calibration-side and is a property of the mechanism, not of the Linear parent; v231 is only 1s faster than v230 (291s vs 292s). So this candidate's expected total is about v234's minus 1s, and it fits inside 300s only if v234's overshoot was at most 1s. The overshoot magnitude is unknown.
sibling_evidence_recorded_after_archivin.effect_on_the_preregistered_rule: none -- the rule is unchanged. The evidence makes its timeout branch the likely one; it does not settle this SHA, because this is a different implementation (different parent) and the overshoot magnitude was never reported.
sibling_evidence_recorded_after_archivin.no_prediction: no seconds and no score are predicted here; the exact overshoot is unknown and side time has no calibrated relationship to the complete package.

side_isolation_reference.note: the +29 is a side-isolation measurement on the v234 source, which is byte-identical to this candidate in its Attention section. Side score does not promote and side time does not predict the full package.

time_risk: A-GR1 adds calibration-side training. The side probe measured +20.7s against the v195 side, and the current complete root sits at 291s against the 300s limit (9s of headroom). The sibling v234 complete package, with 8s of headroom and the same calibration-side cost, was then reported as an official TIMEOUT. Side time has no calibrated relationship to the full package, so the only way to learn this candidate's real number is an official reading; the submission's expected value is now low and the user may reasonably decide not to spend it. A timeout closes this implementation only.
recommended_next_attention_action: the evidence now says the block on A-GR1 is time headroom (about 20s is needed against 9s available), not the parent and not the mechanism. The highest-value Attention work is therefore to reclaim calibration/complete-package seconds first -- the same direction the Linear runtime cards (v233 L-TF1, already officially priced at -4s, and v235 L-AD1) are taking -- and only then land A-GR1. Re-running A-GR1 variants is not a route: weakening it (fewer steps, fewer windows, fewer candidates) is forbidden by the card's own rules.
note: v236 is a descendant of the v231 root. It carries v231's K=2 arm but not the pending v235 (Linear L-AD1) or v233 (L-TF1) changes, so it is not additive with either. The Attention mechanism itself is v234's, unchanged; v234 was built on the v230 root and this is the same block on the v231 root. The score was never at stake here: the six-shard run reproduced v234 item by item (+0.003845 equal-weight, 21/3/48, layers 15 and 22 accepting), so the archived candidate is the same Attention behaviour on a new Linear parent, not new mechanism evidence. Only the second was at stake, and it did not fall inside the limit.
side_value_unaffected: The side-isolation reading (14455/263.7s, +29/+20.7s against the v195 side baseline) is untouched by this timeout. It prices the SCORE of a smaller package; this timeout closes the LANDABILITY of the complete package. The expressiveness gradient (diagonal 0 < triangular 0 < symmetric full matrix +22 < general matrix +29) remains officially confirmed, and A-GR1 remains the third-largest officially positive Attention mechanism after C76.4 (+84) and A1 (+60).
no_variance_inference: The official channel returned only 'timeout', twice now. Nothing was reported about by how much, so no inference is drawn about the official clock's variance and no conversion factor between local and official seconds is derived. The two timeouts agreeing in direction is recorded as 'not contradictory', not as a coefficient.
